reason: E1 and E2 support the feasibility of high-temperature vapor synthesis and the role of mixing entropy/partial pressure in forming homogeneous HEA nanoparticles, but neither addresses premelting/melting behavior or thermal stability. E3 is about mechanical properties of bulk Al-containing HEAs and does not support any premise. The link between synthesis conditions, homogeneity, and thermal response is unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Mixing entropy and reduced partial pressure of constituent elements in the vapor phase enable homogeneous solid solution formation in HEA nanoparticles
High-temperature (>4000 K) vapor synthesis with rapid quenching can produce HEA nanoparticles
Synthesis conditions (plasma gas composition, cooling rate) influence nanoparticle nucleation and growth
Homogeneous solid solution nanoparticles exhibit improved thermal stability (premelting/melting behavior)
Single-metal vapor nanoparticles serve as a valid baseline for comparing thermal behavior
